title: Optimal-rate regret bound for Hedge
statement:
Consider the Hedge algorithm run on $N > 1$ experts over $T > 0$ rounds against a valid loss sequence $\ell$, that is, one with $0 \le \ell_t(i) \le 1$ for every round $t$ and expert $i$. Suppose $2\ln N \le T$, and run Hedge with the learning rate $\eta^* = \sqrt{2\ln N / T}$. Then the regret—the learner's total expected loss minus the loss of the best single expert in hindsight—satisfies
\[
  R_T(\eta^*) \;\le\; \sqrt{2\,T\ln N}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: learning rate equals the optimal η* = sqrt(2 ln N / T)
replaced:
If $T \ge 2\ln N$ (so that $\eta^* \le 1$), then for any valid loss sequence,
\[
  R_T(\eta^*) \;\le\; \sqrt{2\,T\ln N}.
\]
